## Description {#details}

<p>Copies from VGPR to SGPR registers are illegal and the register coalescer will sometimes generate these illegal copies in situations like this:</p>


<p><a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/register">Register</a> Class &lt;vsrc&gt; is the union of &lt;vgpr&gt; and &lt;sgpr&gt;</p>


<p>BB0: %0 &lt;sgpr&gt; = SCALAR_INST %1 &lt;vsrc&gt; = COPY %0 &lt;sgpr&gt; ... BRANCH cond BB1, BB2 BB1: %2 &lt;vgpr&gt; = VECTOR_INST %3 &lt;vsrc&gt; = COPY %2 &lt;vgpr&gt; BB2: %4 &lt;vsrc&gt; = PHI %1 &lt;vsrc&gt;, &lt;bb.0&gt;, %3 &lt;vrsc&gt;, &lt;bb.1&gt; %5 &lt;vgpr&gt; = VECTOR_INST %4 &lt;vsrc&gt;</p>


<p>The coalescer will begin at BB0 and eliminate its copy, then the resulting code will look like this:</p>


<p>BB0: %0 &lt;sgpr&gt; = SCALAR_INST ... BRANCH cond BB1, BB2 BB1: %2 &lt;vgpr&gt; = VECTOR_INST %3 &lt;vsrc&gt; = COPY %2 &lt;vgpr&gt; BB2: %4 &lt;sgpr&gt; = PHI %0 &lt;sgpr&gt;, &lt;bb.0&gt;, %3 &lt;vsrc&gt;, &lt;bb.1&gt; %5 &lt;vgpr&gt; = VECTOR_INST %4 &lt;sgpr&gt;</p>


<p>Now that the result of the PHI instruction is an SGPR, the register allocator is now forced to constrain the register class of %3 to &lt;sgpr&gt; so we end up with final code like this:</p>


<p>BB0: %0 &lt;sgpr&gt; = SCALAR_INST ... BRANCH cond BB1, BB2 BB1: %2 &lt;vgpr&gt; = VECTOR_INST %3 &lt;sgpr&gt; = COPY %2 &lt;vgpr&gt; BB2: %4 &lt;sgpr&gt; = PHI %0 &lt;sgpr&gt;, &lt;bb.0&gt;, %3 &lt;sgpr&gt;, &lt;bb.1&gt; %5 &lt;vgpr&gt; = VECTOR_INST %4 &lt;sgpr&gt;</p>


<p>Now this code contains an illegal copy from a VGPR to an SGPR.</p>


<p>In order to avoid this problem, this pass searches for PHI instructions which define a &lt;vsrc&gt; register and constrains its definition class to &lt;vgpr&gt; if the user of the PHI's definition register is a vector instruction. If the PHI's definition class is constrained to &lt;vgpr&gt; then the coalescer will be unable to perform the COPY removal from the above example which ultimately led to the creation of an illegal COPY.</p>
